label: Yellow & Blue
_shapeNote: TWO MONSTERS, ONE ATTACKER, NO CUT CONTENT IN THE DISPATCHER. (1) Encounter 222 (gml_GlobalScript_scr_encountersetup.gml:839-850) puts obj_blue_enemy in monster slot 0 (monstertype 115) and obj_yellow_enemy in slot 1 (monstertype 116); the battle is started by gml_Object_obj_ch5_DWCL03_Step_0.gml:527 `scr_battle(222, 3, bluecopy, yellowcopy);`. (2) `enemy` is obj_blue_enemy because ALL FOUR monsterattackname announcements in this fight live in gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:162/170/178/186 — obj_yellow_enemy never announces an attack anywhere in the chapter. No extraAttackFiles are needed. (3) Blue wins the enemy turn every time via scr_attackpriority, so Yellow's own mnfight-1.5 block is dead while Blue lives; see mechanics. (4) The chooser is a strict round robin, so the REAL roster equals the dispatcher 4-for-4 — this is the rare fight where the usual dispatcher-overcounts problem does not apply. The two `cut` entries are dbulletcontroller branches for Blue's PROTOTYPE attack (obj_attack_blue_ponddancing) that no code in Chapter 5 can ever select. (5) The fight is WON BY A COURTROOM MINIGAME, not by damage — see mechanics and engineNeeds item 6.
_boxBlockNote: Slices gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:106-145 inclusive. The anchor is UNIQUE in the file (verified: exactly one match) and is the HEALING-RAIN GATE, not the growtangle creation — the creation is its `else if` at :108-109, so anchoring one statement earlier is what keeps the healing-rain turn correct (on that turn NO box is created at all). The endAnchor at :146 is also unique. Do NOT anchor on `if (!instance_exists(obj_growtangle))`: that string appears at :108 with a leading `else `, and starting there drops the gate. The four per-attack box tweaks (myattackchoice 0/1/2/3 at :111-144) are all inside the slice, so one slice serves every attack: choice 0 shifts box and heart x -= 50; choice 1 sets maxxscale 3.5 and y += 48; choice 2 shifts x -= 50 and maxxscale 3; choice 3 sets maxxscale 3. Everything in the slice short-circuits safely if obj_yellow_enemy is absent (the `i_ex(obj_yellow_enemy) &&` guard) — but the excluded line :146 does NOT guard its `obj_yellow_enemy.healingraincon` read, which is one reason a Yellow stub is required (engineNeeds item 1).
_turnBlockNote: The endAnchor is a bare `}` ON PURPOSE, exactly as in aqua_seth.json. `scr_turntimer(90);` is the LAST statement of the mnfight==1.5 block (gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:150) and the very next token is that block's closing brace at :151, so `}` resolves unambiguously and the slice is the single line `scr_turntimer(90);`. That is the FLOOR, not the real turn length: this fight has NO separate turn-length ladder. Every real turntimer is written INSIDE its own dispatcher branch (:165 = 300, :173 = 270, :181 = 225, :189 = 300), so gen_attacks.js's per-attack `setup` slice already carries it. Do NOT move the turn anchor onto the dispatcher — that would replay `scr_bulletspawner` and double every controller (the documented Knight trap). scr_turntimer only RAISES, so replaying the 90 floor and the per-attack value in either order is safe. `scr_turntimer(90);` is the first of five scr_turntimer calls in the file and extractTurnBlock takes the first match whose next 80 chars contain `turntimer` — the anchor text itself satisfies that, so the match is :150.

No writer for 130 exists anywhere in Chapter 5; see the type-129 note. gml_Object_obj_attack_blue_ponddancing_Draw_0.gml references obj_enemy_yellow_example, obj_enemy_blue_attack and obj_attack_yellow_reticle, all parentless dev-template objects that nothing ever instance_creates — confirming this is the prototype version of Blue's fight, not shipped content.

mechanics:
TWO ENEMY OBJECTS, ONE ATTACKER. Encounter 222 (gml_GlobalScript_scr_encountersetup.gml:839-850) puts obj_blue_enemy in monster slot 0 (monstertype 115, at camera + (466, 40)) and obj_yellow_enemy in slot 1 (monstertype 116, at camera + (500, 160)); started by gml_Object_obj_ch5_DWCL03_Step_0.gml:527 `scr_battle(222, 3, bluecopy, yellowcopy);`. Both are 2060 HP / AT 16 / DF 0 / 450 gold / sparepoint 0 / mercymax 100 (gml_GlobalScript_scr_monstersetup.gml:455-465 for Blue, :469-480 for Yellow) — sparepoint 0 means neither can ever be spared by mercy.

BLUE OWNS THE ENEMY TURN. During enemytalk Yellow sets myattackpriority = 0 and Blue sets myattackpriority = 1 (gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Step_0.gml:8, gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:52), and both then call scr_attackpriority(myattackpriority - 1), leaving obj_battlecontroller.attackpriority at 0. gml_GlobalScript_scr_attackpriority.gml returns true only when the stored value is STRICTLY LESS than the argument, so at global.mnfight == 1.5 Yellow's scr_attackpriority(0) fails and Blue's scr_attackpriority(1) succeeds. attackpriority is seeded to -1 in gml_Object_obj_battlecontroller_Create_0.gml:30 and reset to -1 every turn (gml_GlobalScript_scr_endturn.gml:114, gml_GlobalScript_scr_mnendturn.gml:28). Yellow's own mnfight-1.5 branch (gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Step_0.gml:98-111) therefore only runs if Blue is gone; it makes a plain camera-centred box with scr_turntimer(90) and NO attack at all. Yellow's bullets-phase branch (:113-162) only increments her own `turns` and writes a battle message — she never sets global.monsterattackname anywhere in the chapter.

CHOOSER: a single line, gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Other_11.gml:1 — `myattackchoice = turns % 4;`. Strict round robin 0,1,2,3,0,... No randomness, no HP gate, no phase gate on attack selection. All four dispatcher branches are reachable, so the REAL roster equals the dispatcher: 4 of 4.

HEALING RAIN IS A TURN REPLACEMENT (no announcement, no controller, no .type). gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:106-107: at mnfight 1.5, if Yellow exists AND is below 50% max HP AND healingraincon == 0, Blue sets obj_yellow_enemy.healingraincon = 1 INSTEAD of creating the box (:108-109 is its else-if). On that turn there is no obj_growtangle, no scr_moveheart (:146 is gated on healingraincon == 0), and the dispatcher never fires because :158 requires healingraincon == 0 — so `turns` does NOT increment (:192 is inside that guard) and the skipped attack simply plays on the next turn. Yellow's Step:438-462 runs the beat: destroy writers, battle text "BLUE cast HEALING RAIN on YELLOW!", instance_create(obj_blue_enemy.x, obj_blue_enemy.y, obj_healing_rain), global.turntimer = 999 while the cloud lives, then global.turntimer = 2 to end the turn. gml_Object_obj_healing_rain_Draw_0.gml:43-44 restores Yellow to full HP; the cloud self-destroys at timer 75 (:59-60). It can repeat on every turn Yellow starts under half HP.

YELLOW BODYGUARDS BLUE. gml_Object_obj_heroparent_Step_0.gml:355-371: if the player's target is obj_blue_enemy, Yellow is teleported to blue.x - 60, global.chartarget is rewritten to Yellow's slot, and Yellow takes the hit with hurtsprite spr_yellow_block and blockcon = 1 (unwound 30 frames later by gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Step_0.gml:421-436). The same interception is duplicated for Rude Buster in gml_Object_obj_rudebuster_anim_Step_0.gml:25-42. Combined with the healing rain, Blue is effectively undamageable and Yellow is effectively unkillable below half HP.

THE FIGHT IS WON BY A COURTROOM MINIGAME, NOT BY DAMAGE. Yellow's ACT 1 is "Justice" (gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Create_0.gml:256-287, `yellow_justice_check`, cost justice_cost = 100 from :18, or the sentinel 2497.5 = greyed out when the relevant EVIDENCE is missing); using it runs gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Step_0.gml:182-242, which creates obj_yellow_trial_manager with trial_id = trial_counter and an evidence_list built from evidence_obtained[0..6] (seeded from scr_keyitemcheck at Create_0:42-48, plus the Annoying Dog fallback at :230 and the Egg at :232-233). Blue's ACT 0 "Evidence" hands out missing EVIDENCE (gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:223-272 -> obj_yellow_enemy.gain_evidence(), defined at Create_0:77-224) and Blue's ACT 1 "Integrity" revives downed party members for half the party's TP (Step_0:290-406). ACT names/costs are installed in gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Other_22.gml.

FOUR TRIALS, FIXED CULPRITS. gml_Object_obj_yellow_trial_manager_Create_0.gml:308-312 builds trial_array[0..3] plus trial_array[99]; the perp enum (declared at the tail of that file) is 0=Aqua, 1=Seth, 2=Green, 3=Blue, 4=Yellow, 5=Flowery, mapped at :2744-2768. Culprits: trial 1 -> Seth (:269), trial 2 -> Green (:280), trial 3 -> Aqua (:291), trial 4 -> BLUE (:302). A wrong accusation runs wrong_accusation (:314): fail_counter++, just_failed = true, and justice_cost drops to 50. A right one runs right_accusation (:531): just_succeeded = true, `trial_counter = scr_approach(trial_counter, 3, 1)`, fail_counter = 0. Those counters drive the per-turn dialogue variants in gml_Object_obj_yellow_enemy_Step_0.gml:16-54 and the battle-message variants at :136-156. Convicting Blue in trial 4 runs right_blue (defined at :1576) and ENDS THE BATTLE OUTRIGHT: :1801 sets obj_battlecontroller.skipvictory = 2 and :1803 calls scr_wincombat(). The manager is NOT exclusive to this fight — obj_flowery_enemy reuses it with trial_id = 99 (gml_Object_obj_flowery_enemy_Step_0.gml:2599-2611), which is why end_trial and begin_trial both branch on `global.encounterno == 222` (:646, :2719).

DEAD CODE INSIDE THE FOUR USED ATTACKS (know this before speccing). (a) obj_enemy_blue_boxspin has a mode 0 and a mode 1; the dispatcher pins `d.mode = 1` (gml_Object_obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:3392) and Create_0:27 also defaults to 1, so mode 0 NEVER RUNS: gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_boxspin_Step_0.gml:36 (`alarm[0] = 96`) is the ONLY place the object's own alarm[0] is ever armed (:95 is an alarm[0] inside `with (obj_attack_blue_dancer_bullet)`, not its own), so Alarm_0, the alarm[0]==64 spin trigger at :118-134, the box-flip block at :136-162, obj_attack_blue_revolver_bullet, Alarm_1, Alarm_2, the `mode == 0` arm of Step_2:3-9 and the spr_blue_boxcover draw in Draw_0:3-4 are all unreachable. Blue's revolver attack exists in code and cannot fire. (b) gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_flower_aim_Create_0.gml:14 pins `spread_type = 3` and nothing in the chapter reassigns it, so the spread_type 0 / 1 / 2 reticle patterns (Step_0:18-70, 72-158, 160-344) are dead; only the three-volleys-of-three up/down/up sweep at Step_0:345-414 plays. (c) gml_Object_obj_blue_singing2_Create_0.gml:31 pins `mode = 2`, so the mode-1 arms (Step_0:87-88, :210+) never run.

TEMPLATE OBJECTS — CONFIRMED EXCLUDED. obj_enemy_blue_example, obj_enemy_yellow_example and obj_enemy_blue_attack are dev testbeds, not fight objects: none has a parent in objects.tsv (the three real Blue attack objects are all obj_bulletparent children), and a chapter-wide grep finds NO instance_create of any of them from anywhere. gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_example_Create_0.gml:8 creates its own obj_growtangle at hardcoded room coordinates (320, 170) with no battle context and then hardcodes x/y to (468, 96). The whole prototype cluster — obj_enemy_blue_example, obj_enemy_yellow_example, obj_enemy_blue_attack, obj_attack_blue_ponddancing, obj_attack_blue_flowerbullet, obj_attack_yellow_reticle, obj_attack_yellow_reticle_bullet — references only itself, and is reachable from live code ONLY through the cut dbulletcontroller types 129/130. The SHIPPED objects with confusingly similar names — obj_enemy_blue_boxspin and obj_enemy_blue_flower_aim — ARE real (dbulletcontroller types 302 and 303).
engineNeeds:
1. obj_yellow_enemy MUST EXIST AS A POSITIONED INSTANCE or two of the four attacks hard-error on an unset instance variable: gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_flower_aim_Create_0.gml:12-13 (`beam_x = obj_yellow_enemy.x; beam_y = obj_yellow_enemy.y + 46;`), its Step_0:11-16 and :420-424 (writes Yellow's idlesprite/image_speed), its Alarm_0:49-50; gml_Object_obj_blue_singing2_Step_0.gml:5-9 and :26-30; and gml_GlobalScript_scr_blue_petal_explosion.gml:22-26, which reads obj_yellow_enemy.x/y for EVERY petal burst and hands them to obj_yellow_beam.setup(). That script is called three times from BlueSinging (gml_Object_obj_blue_singing2_Step_0.gml:121/160/199). The excluded box-block line :146 also reads obj_yellow_enemy.healingraincon unguarded. A stub at encountersetup's coordinates (camera + (500, 160), gml_GlobalScript_scr_encountersetup.gml:846-847) with a `myself` slot, `healingraincon = 0`, and a global.monsterhp/monstermaxhp entry is enough.
2. TURN LENGTH IS LOAD-BEARING AND LIVES IN THE DISPATCHER BRANCH. Each branch calls scr_turntimer(300 / 270 / 225 / 300) immediately after dc.type, so it arrives with each attack's `setup` slice; the turnBlock declared here carries only the raise-only floor scr_turntimer(90) from :150. THREE of the four attacks read global.turntimer to schedule their exit: gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_boxspin_Step_0.gml:105 (<= 30, dancer flies home), gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_flower_aim_Step_0.gml:416 (<= 20, restores Yellow's idle sprite and ends), gml_Object_obj_blue_singing2_Step_0.gml:24 (<= 30, lerps back to Blue and stops firing). At the studio's 90-frame floor all three would fire their ending on frame one. GuidedBullet (301) is the exception: obj_blue_guidelines has no self-terminating condition at all (Step_0 is 45 lines and just extends the chain every 3 frames) and relies entirely on turn-end cleanup.
3. BOX HANDLING IS UNUSUAL — attacks write obj_growtangle directly rather than going through maxxscale. gml_Object_obj_blue_guidelines_Create_0.gml:4-8 sets obj_growtangle.image_xscale/image_yscale = 2.5 DIRECTLY, bypassing the grow animation. gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_boxspin_Step_0.gml:19-22 lerps image_xscale 3.5 -> 3.6 and image_yscale 2 -> 1.85 at timer 24 (against the maxxscale = 3.5 set in the box block at :126). gml_Object_obj_enemy_blue_boxspin_Step_2.gml:11-29 moves obj_growtangle.y on a sine every frame and drags obj_heart AND every obj_attack_blue_dancer_bullet with it, re-clamping the heart to scr_get_box(0..3). The engine needs a growtangle whose x / y / image_xscale / image_yscale are externally writable, plus scr_get_box(0..5) and scr_afterimagefast on it.
4. SUPPORT NATIVES used by these four attacks: scr_fire_bullet, scr_bullet_init, scr_bullet_inherit, scr_bulletspawner, scr_darksize, scr_lerpvar, scr_script_delayed, scr_script_repeat, scr_var, scr_var_delay, scr_approach, scr_ease_towards_direction, scr_afterimagefast, scr_doom, scr_get_box, ds_list_* (guidelines, flower_aim and singing all keep ds_lists), instance_create_depth, point_direction/point_distance/lengthdir_*, and d_line_width_color. obj_yellow_beam needs its Create-defined `setup(x1, y1, x2, y2, width, width_goal, circle_width, beam_lifetime, circle_lifetime)` method (gml_Object_obj_yellow_beam_Create_0.gml:18-30). obj_blue_flower_reticle drives itself off an Other_10 that converts xgoal/ygoal into speed+direction (gml_Object_obj_blue_flower_reticle_Other_10.gml:1-2). gml_Object_obj_blue_singing2_Draw_0.gml draws up to 3 x 112 d_line_width_color segments per frame (:3-17) — a per-frame cost worth watching.
5. NO SOUL-MODE CHANGE. The fight is plain RED soul throughout (scr_moveheart at gml_Object_obj_blue_enemy_Step_0.gml:146-147). No green/purple/yellow soul controller is created anywhere in either enemy.
6. NOT MODELLED BY THE BULLET ENGINE AT ALL: the courtroom trial (obj_yellow_trial_manager — a 2790-line Create plus Step/Draw/Alarm/CleanUp — obj_trial_perp, evidence key items via scr_keyitemcheck, obj_balloon_queue / msgset_add speech balloons, obj_face, and spr_kris_lawyer / spr_susie_lawyer / spr_ralsei_lawyer battle-sprite swaps) and the healing-rain turn. Both are turn REPLACEMENTS in the Pink-dates sense: no monsterattackname, no controller, no .type — an announcement scan cannot find either, and each needs a bespoke driver. The trial is also the fight's ONLY win condition (scr_wincombat at gml_Object_obj_yellow_trial_manager_Create_0.gml:1803), so a damage-only harness will never end this battle.
7. The four attacks all hide the boss: obj_enemy_blue_boxspin_Create_0.gml:4-5, obj_enemy_blue_flower_aim_Create_0.gml:3-4 and obj_blue_singing2_Create_0.gml:6-7 each set `obj_blue_enemy.visible = false` and adopt its depth/image_index. A studio that draws the boss unconditionally will double-draw Blue for three of the four attacks.
